title: Your income has stopped with no warning
lede: Contract ended, client gone, hours cut to nothing, or dismissal. The money coming in is now zero or close to it, and the outgoings have not noticed.

blocks.text: Contract ended, client gone, hours cut to nothing, or dismissal. The money coming in is now zero or close to it, and the outgoings have not noticed.

items: The first mistake is almost always cutting the wrong things — the small comforts — while leaving the large fixed costs untouched. Fixed costs are where the actual runway is.
The second is silence. Creditors, landlords, and utilities have hardship processes, but only for people who make contact.
The third is treating this as a personal failure and therefore a secret. Secrecy delays the practical steps by weeks.
You almost certainly have entitlements you do not know about, and they usually run from the date you claim, not the date you needed them.

items.move: Calculate your runway in weeks, not vibes
items.detail: Available cash divided by essential monthly outgoings. One number. It converts dread into a plan.

items.move: Split outgoings into essential, contractual, and optional
items.detail: Housing, energy, food, transport, insurance are essential. Subscriptions, upgrades, and credit extras are not.

items.move: Claim everything you are entitled to today
items.detail: Unemployment support, housing help, council reductions, child-related support. Payments usually start from the claim date, so delay is money lost permanently.

items.move: Contact every fixed creditor before missing anything
items.detail: Mortgage, rent, energy, phone, loans. Ask for a payment holiday or reduced plan. Pre-emptive calls get better outcomes than post-default ones.
Housing and energy before consumer debt. Do not let a loud creditor reorder your priorities.

items.move: Start income generation in week one
items.detail: Any income, including partial or temporary. Momentum matters more than matching your old salary immediately.

items.say: "My income stopped on the 14th. I want to arrange a payment holiday or reduced payments before I miss anything. What are my options and can you confirm in writing?"
"I am in financial hardship. Please put me on your hardship register and tell me about payment plans and grants."
"I am available from Monday, I do X, and I am looking for anything from three weeks upward. If you hear of something, send it my way."
"Here are the actual numbers. This is what we are cutting and this is how long we have. I would rather we both knew."

items: Payday loans, credit card cash advances, and buy-now-pay-later to plug the hole.
Cashing in pensions or long-term savings in week one, before checking entitlements and concessions.
Hiding it from your household. They will find out later and the delay costs real money.
Waiting for the perfect replacement role while the runway burns.
Cancelling insurance to save a little. One uninsured event ends the plan.
Rebuild one month of essentials as your first savings goal, before anything else.
Keep the leaner budget for three months after income returns. That is where the buffer comes from.
Write down what you cut and never missed. It is usually a surprising amount.
Diversify: a second client, a second skill, a second income stream. Single points of failure are the real problem being revealed here.

limit: Contact creditors before you miss a payment, not after — you have far more options while you are still current. Do not take a high-cost short-term loan to cover a shortfall, and do not touch a pension early without regulated advice. Free debt advice charities exist in most countries; use one before any commercial "debt solution" company.
